"Over all people is our God." 44.text: In the general church rubric, not a single instance is encountered of a Saint with an All-Night Vigil falling in an Afterfeast on a Sunday, except in the midst of the feasts of Pentecost; but because the feasts of Pentecost have separate rubrics, when some Saint with an All-Night Vigil falls in the midst of Pentecost, then the rubric for him must be taken from the third part of this Typikon. However, in time, this case may happen even outside the feasts of Pentecost and a need for a separate rubric will arise; therefore, for the sake of this, we add these two cases to the instances of feasts: that is, a Saint with an All-Night Vigil on a Sunday and on weekdays, and their rubric may serve also in the case of a Patronal Saint.

45.text: According to the ancient rubric, a saint "on 4" could be of two types: that is, either with a troparion or without a troparion; and when the saint has no troparion, then at Matins, instead of "God is the Lord," "Alleluia" was sung and the divine service had a separate rubric. But in our current Horologia, troparia are given for every day of the month, and therefore at Matins we always sing "God is the Lord," and we limit the "Alleluia" service to Great Lent, as do the Greeks. 66.text: Lviv Synod in heading 5. According to the Typikon given at the end of our Apostles, and in our previous ones, as also in some Greek service books in Goar, the daily antiphons "It is good" are given, also on Sundays, with the refrain only Sunday on the 3rd antiphon, as the Italo-Greeks also observe. General Greek service books give the Typika on Sunday, and Octoechoi also on weekdays; for in them are given daily stichera on the "Beatitudes", by which is understood the presence of the Typika. With such a difference of typikons let everyone preserve the custom of his Church, and among us the Typikon is -- of the Synod. In vain during the Synod some tried, saying, that to take daily antiphons, instead of the Typika, does not correspond to our rite; for daily antiphons are given not only by the aforementioned service books and apostles, but also by Greek Readers [Anagnostiki] and the Moscow Typikon in chapter 25, and St. Sophronius himself, Patriarch of Jerusalem, in the 7th century, in the explanation of the Divine Liturgy (Spicileg. Rom. tom. 4, nn. 12, 13, 14. Propag. 1840) -- mentions nothing about the Typika, but only about the antiphons "It is good". About the Typika we assume that they were left for the case when there is no Liturgy. For in the beginning numerous in monasticism were of the laity, who could not serve the Holy Liturgy; and therefore, instead of the Liturgy, they had to use the Order of Typika; therefore also the Synod limits them to days in which there is no Liturgy, so that in this way the memory of them was preserved only in monasteries. It is equally good to use antiphons, as also the Typika, when it is taken fully; but when from every psalm only one verse is taken and without stichera on the "Beatitudes", as they practice, then it is better to use antiphons. Finally, the full Typika is quite long and in present times was shortened.

71.text: Since the Octoechos gives 6 stichera, and the Typikon does not determine which 3 of the 6 to take, we leave this to the judgment of the Reader. However, to say how it is better, let us first recall that the daily service of the Octoechos is double, that is: on Monday -- Penitential and to the Bodiless [Powers], on Tuesday -- Penitential and to the Forerunner, on Wednesday and Friday -- to the Cross and the Theotokos, on Thursday -- to the Apostles and Nicholas, on Saturday -- to all Saints and the Departed. Thus, in order not to discard either of the two services of the weekday, the Greek Octoechos (Παρακλητική /Parakletike/), printed in the "Propaganda" in 1738, gives from the three stichera of the first service only the two first stichera, and from the three stichera of the second service -- only one, the first. Among us, so that the printed stichera given in the Octoechos do not remain in vain, it would be possible to sing alternating all three stichera of the first service and all three stichera of the second service, that is, one year, odd -- three of the first service, and the second year, even -- three of the second service, or, even better -- one year two first stichera of the first service and one sticheron, the first, of the second service, and the second year -- one sticheron, the third, of the first service and two last of the second service. The Greek Typikon takes nothing from the Octoechos, but only three stichera from the Menaion on 6, repeating each (Καιφ. ε /chapter 5/). The Moscow Typikon takes three first stichera of the Theotokos from the Octoechos, which do not exist in our editions, but we find them in the Greek-Venetian edition; the Moscow Octoechos of 1782 has the same stichera as ours.

72.text: In the Greek Menaion after the Doxastikon to the saint his Theotokion is also added. If there is no Doxastikon, then only certain most general Theotokia of the Octoechos are indicated by initial words; it is implied that they are known, although the number of Octoechos editions makes their search inconvenient. We cite here some: 1. Θεοτόκε, συ ει ο άμπελος "O Theotokos, Thou Art the vine" (Venetian Octoechos, Tone 6, on the Aposticha); θεον σαρκοΰεντα εκ σου "God incarnate from Thee" (Tone 6, on Saturday, Praises, Moscow edition); Δέσποινα προσδεξαι "O Sovereign Lady, receive" (Tone 8, on Saturday at Matins; Την πασαν ελπίδα "All my hope" (Tone 2, on Thursday, on the Aposticha of Matins). Sometimes the Theotokion is not indicated even by initial words, but is only named generally: θεοτοκιον ομοιον /Theotokion similar/, or only: θεοτοκιον /Theotokion/ (Menaion September 3, August 2); in this case one must select a Theotokion from the Octoechos. Four aforementioned Theotokia are given also on "Lord, I have cried", and on the Aposticha (Menaion November 1 and 3, December 5, July 1). In the last edition of the Venetian Menaion Theotokia are given almost always fully. But among us, at the end of every volume of the Menaion are given all Theotokia that are taken on "Lord, I have cried" and on the Aposticha, and not only for every tone, but also for every day of the week, in order not to repeat the same Theotokia many times. In the Pochaiv Anthologion Theotokia are given only according to the tone, and not also according to the day; and in general services sometimes only the first words are cited, and they themselves are not given.

77.text: When two kathismata should be read, and when three, we noted in the note to the Order of Daily Matins on page 41. Regarding small litanies which are read between kathismata and sessional hymns, the Lviv Synod, our Horologions and our Sluzhebnyky (at the end) give them also at Small Matins, and they are used also by the Greek-Melkites (according to the testimony of their patriarch bl. m. Clement Bahous). Conversely, in the Russian Typikon, approved by their Governing Synod (Moscow edition of 1859), in the Order of Daily Matins it is written that the Priest says them only at the Vigil and when the memory of saints having a Polyeleos and Doxology is celebrated; similarly also in the new Wallachian-Bucharest Typikon, in which in the Order of Daily Matins is given: "We take sessional hymns from the Octoechos without litanies" (untranslatable); and adds: "In monasteries, usually, between kathismata litanies are taken only on Sunday and when more special saints occur". From the Greek Typikon no conclusion can be made, for in it small litanies are not mentioned neither at Small Matins, nor at Great, nor before the Canon, nor after the Canon. It is assumed in the Typikon that this is known to everyone. From the rubrics of the Greek Triodion, given at Matins on Meatfare Saturday, one can conclude that these litanies should be said also at Small Matins. For it gives: η συνηιϊης στιχολογια. Εν δε ταις συναπταις πασαις της στιχολογιας και του Κανόνος, μνημονεύονται πάντες οι προαπελΰοντες Πατέρες και αδελφοί ημων /Ordinary Stichology. In all small litanies of the Stichology and of the Canon, all our fathers and brethren who have passed away before us are commemorated/. Let everyone observe the rubric and custom of his Church. Finally, in our opinion, later typikons reject litanies here only for the sake of greater shortening of the divine service; if the single difference between Small and Great Matins were the rejection or use of litanies, then this difference should have been indicated in some place of ancient liturgical books; however, this is not encountered. What the exclamation of the third litany should be is not indicated in any of the church books. Therefore we are forced to borrow it from Great Matins. At Great Matins in Slavonic books two exclamations are given which are used at the third litany, that is one -- for Sunday "For blessed is" and the second -- for Polyeleos feasts "For holy Art Thou". For the sake of distinguishing the Sunday day from the ordinary day, at Small Matins it is appropriate to use the second "For holy Art Thou", although it would not be bad to use also the first "For blessed is" (Οτι ευλογητοα), for in Greek books we find only this one exclamation, without distinction of day. Regarding Sessional Hymns, they are taken two or three after each stichology, depending on the edition, except the Theotokion. In Lviv editions of the Octoechos and in the Greek-Venetian one, only to the Theotokion is sung "Glory, Both now". In the Pochaiv and Moscow ones a separate refrain is also given to every second, or even to the third sessional hymn. This refrain, corresponding to the content of the sessional hymn: on Monday and Tuesday -- Penitential "O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger"; on Wednesday and Friday -- of the Cross, and on Thursday -- of the Apostles; to the third sessional hymn, that is the Martyron -- also the Martyron refrain: "Wondrous is God in His saints".

91.text: The Greek Typikon gives the whole service only to the saint, and Apostle and Gospel -- first of the day, and then of the saint; Προκειμενον του κατά την ημεραν Αγιου, Αλληλούια του Αγιου, Ευαγγελιον της ημέρας και του Αγιου. (Καιφ. σ) /Prokimenon of the saint of the day, Alleluia of the saint, Gospel of the day and of the saint (chapter 6)/. So also in chapter 99, Mark. Although this rubric is given only in the Saturday service, however, it must be understood that also on other days of the week it should be so. Slavonic typikons prescribe the whole service to the day and to the saint, if he has one, and troparia -- also to the temple, if it is of the Lord or of the Theotokos. The Moscow Typikon also prescribes to the temple, if the temple is of a saint (although this does not agree with the rubric of that same Typikon, given on September 26 and January 30); this same Typikon ends the Kontakia with the Kontakion for the Dead "With the saints give rest" with the refrain "Glory" and the Kontakion of the temple, if it is of the Lord or of the Theotokos, if -- not, then with the usual "Protection" ("O Undisputed Intercessor") with the refrain "Both now" (chapter 52). This custom we find also among Greek-Italians and Greek-Melkites, but it does not exist among Constantinopolitan Greeks and Athonites, with the exception of some. But, since according to the rubric of the Greek Typikon, two Apostles and two Gospels were to be taken, and according to the Slavonic rubric, also the whole service of the day and of the saint, if he has one, and, since many saints (over one hundred eighty) have an Apostle and Gospel, as follows from the content of the Apostle-Gospel, therefore, in order to shorten the duration of the divine service, followers of the Greek Rite began already many years ago to reject certain rubrics; therefore also our Ruthenians take at the Liturgy only the service of the day, and reject the saint without Polyeleos; some -- conversely: take only the service to the saint, and reject the service of the day, as evidenced by the Pochaiv Sluzhebnik of 1765, which gives the Apostle and Gospel only on Sundays, and on weekdays -- only in Bright Week and in the week after the Descent of the Holy Spirit, similarly as Latin Missals, which give the Apostle and Gospel of the day only in these two mentioned weeks, for Great Lent and for certain other days. This custom we find also among Greek-Italians, observed also by some of those who are called Orthodox, whom the Moscow Typikon accuses, saying: "The Ecumenical Church does not take neither on the Beatitudes, nor at Liturgies the Apostle and Gospel to the saint on every day, only the sequential, that is the pillar throughout the whole year, in sequence, as also of selected saints who have an Apostle and Gospel. And if the Apostle and Gospel of the saint is read every day, then this is from one's own ignorance, and not according to the church typikon" (chapter 58, at the end). Exactly so also in the manuscript of the three-hundred-year-old Gospel that is among us. However, this rubric of the Ecumenical Church is not observed by the Constantinopolitan Hierarch, called Ecumenical, nor by the Churches subject to him, who (according to the testimony of hierarch Benjamin Νεαπολεος /of Neapolis/, who lived in Constantinople and on Mount Athos, who in our times accepted church union) have the custom, also in monasteries, to take the Apostle and Gospel only of the day, if the saint does not have one, if he has, then only to the saint, and in another they adhere to the new Constantinopolitan Typikon, printed in the patriarchal typography in 1851, marked with the patriarchal seal and confirmed by signatures of all patriarchs and hierarchs subject to them. In this Typikon there, where the rubric gives two Apostles and Gospels, one Apostle-Gospel is given, that is the Apostle -- of the first service, and the Gospel -- of the second service. Thus e. g. October 26, November 21, when they fall on a Sunday and on John the Theologian May 8, when it falls on Ascension.

197.text: About the commemoration of the feast at the Dismissal in the Afterfeast we find nothing in Greek typikons. From the Typikon of Slavonic Triodia and of the Moscow Typikon one could conclude that the commemoration of the feast should be taken only on the very solemn day of the feast and on its Apodosis. For it prescribes to take the Paschal Dismissal throughout the whole Bright Week, every day of which has the form of the divine service of the very day of the Resurrection, and afterwards prescribes to take it at the Liturgy of the Apodosis of the Resurrection. However, today we observe the general custom to make the festal commemoration also on other days of the Afterfeast, which has also the rubric of the Sluzhebnik, printed in Stratyn under the Lviv Bishop Gedeon Balaban in 1604, 11 years before the Tserkovne Oko, which gives the following: "Know, that festal dismissals are taken from the day of the feast until the Apodosis of the feast of every day" (page 517). Similarly one could take in Theotokion Afterfeasts, but the words "today" and "solemnly" must be discarded. However, in Afterfeasts of the Lord it is better not to take the commemoration of the feast on Sunday, for it does not combine well with the Sunday commemoration, which must occupy the first place. It would be, e. g. on the Afterfeast of the Nativity of Christ: "Who rose from the dead and Who was born in a cavern in Bethlehem of Judea and let Himself be laid in a manger for our salvation, Christ, our true God". And on weekdays, except Sunday, the commemoration of the feast can be taken without doubt, for then the service of the feast replaces the service of the Octoechos and therefore, instead of the commemoration of the service of the day, that is of the Octoechos, it is good to take the commemoration of the service of the feast. Some on Sunday discard the Sunday commemoration and take only of the feast, but they act contrary to our Sluzhebnyky, which on the Sunday of the Holy Fathers, in the middle of the feast of the Ascension before Pentecost, give the Sunday commemoration.

201.text: According to the most general and most ancient typikons in the Afterfeast and on the Apodosis the Trisagion should be taken, and not "As many as have been baptized into Christ" or "Before Thy Cross", for they are taken on the very day of the feast, with the exception of "As many as have been baptized into Christ", which is taken not only on the very day of the Resurrection, but also throughout the whole Bright Week, since throughout the whole Bright Week the divine service takes place as on the very day of the Resurrection. On other days, until the Apodosis of the Resurrection, the Trisagion is taken. So have the general Greek and Slavonic typikons and the most ancient Typikon of the Monastery of St. Nicholas of Casole in the district of Otranto, kept in the Barberini library in Rome, written six hundred or seven hundred years ago. In it on fol. 121 and 124 is given the Typikon, which I gave. With this general and ancient typikon one Greek Typikon does not agree, written by the Reverend Father Bartholomew, a companion of the Reverend Father Nilus and co-founder of the Monastery of Grottaferrata near Rome, kept in that same monastery, which prescribes "As many as have been baptized into Christ" until the Apodosis of the feast. E. g. December 26 gives: Και αντί του Τρισάγιου Οσοι εις Χριστον. Τούτο γαρ λεγομεν έως ου αποδιδοται η εορτή /And instead of the Trisagion As many as have been baptized into Christ. For this we say until the feast is taken leave of/. Does not agree also the new Constantinopolitan Typikon 1851, marked with the seal of the Patriarch. See, e. g. on Monday of the Holy Spirit there, where Greek and Slavonic Triodia have the Trisagion, this Typikon has "As many as have been baptized into Christ". Regarding Troparia, Mark thus: Sunday, Glory: Troparion to the saint, if he has, Both now: Kontakion of the feast (Καιφ. ξε)/chapter 65/.

254.text: This renovation, in Greek Εγκαίνια /renovation/, in Latin Dedicatio, or Dedication of the temple of the Resurrection of Christ, built in Jerusalem on Golgotha under Emperor Constantine in the year 335.

255.text: The Tserkovne Oko and our handwritten typikon do not give this first kontakion of the Renovation. But the Greek-Venetian Menaion gives it after the 6th ode; also we do not find the kontakion of the Cross, nor the kontakion of Cornelius in any edition, but only in our horologion and the Greek one of the Propaganda, and of the cross also in the Tserkovne Oko; the well-written typikon of the XVII century of the Lviv University library (1. N. 4), our handwritten typikon and the Greek-Venetian Menaion do not give either a troparion or a kontakion to the saint.

256.text: The Tserkovne Oko (in the menologion, fol. 268), and after it the Moscow Typikon (fol. 54, on the reverse) give at the hours only the Troparion of the Renovation and Glory: to the Forefeast, kontakia to the Renovation and to the Forefeast -- alternating, and to the saint -- nothing. We think that this rule will be good if the saint does not have a troparion and kontakion. In those editions where a troparion and kontakion to the saint are given, there is no reason not to take them at the hours.

257.text: Thus we consider; for in the case when the typikon does not give the Kontakion of the Forefeast, this one is added later.

259.text: More simply, according to the ancient rule, the cross with basil is placed on a tray. Today's Greeks more often, instead of basil, place flowers under the cross.

260.text: According to the Slavic typikon -- also a phelonion.

261.text: According to our custom -- on a pillow.

263.text: In the Greek Typikon and the Slavic one of the Lviv University nothing is said about this bringing out of the precious Cross, except the Troparion "Save, O Lord"; Απέρχεται ο Ιερεύς και ο Εκκλησιαρχης συν τω Κανδηλαπτη εν τω σκευοφυλακιω μετά λαμπάδων και θυμιατών, και λαμβανουσιν το τιμιον ξυλον του Σταυρου, ψάλλοντες και το Τροπαριον Σωσον Κύριε τον λαον σου, και φερουσιν εις την Εκκλησιαν, και επιτνθεασιν αυτό επάνω της αγίας Τραπέζης, και απτει κηρος έμπροσθεν αυτό επάνω της αγίας Τραπέζης, και απτει κηρος έμπροσθεν δι όλης της νυκτός/The Priest and the Ecclesiarch with the lamp-lighter go to the sacristy with candles and censers and take the precious wood of the Cross, singing the troparion "Save, O Lord, Thy people", carry it to the church and place it on the holy table, and a candle is lit before it for the whole night/. (14 September). The beginning is usual and other preparatory prayers, that is Trisagion with "Our Father", as later Slavic typikons give, longer than this entire order, for it consists only of one Troparion of the Cross, and with the Slavic addition, also of a Kontakion.

264.text: Ancient Greek typikons mention nothing about a Deacon, neither at the bringing out, nor at the exaltation, nor at the laying of the precious Cross, but only about one priest. The Greek typikon, similarly to the Slavic ones, prescribes for the Priest to vest in all priestly vestments: αλασσει ο Ιερεύς πασαν την ιερατικην στολην /the Priest vests in all priestly vestments/. The Greek Triodion (Sunday of the Veneration of the Cross) and the new Constantinopolitan Typikon, similarly to Slavic typikons, prescribes for the Priest to enter with the cross from the sanctuary to the temple through the northern doors: εκ του αριστερού Βήματος /from the left side of the sanctuary/. Greek typikons, with the exception of the new Constantinopolitan, and the Slavic of the Lviv University, prescribe for the Priest, having exited from the sanctuary to the temple, to head to the entrance doors that lead from the temple to the narthex, which are sometimes called royal, and there await the end of the Doxology and from there exclaim "Wisdom, attend", and then head to the tetrapod, which is before the iconostasis. Although these doors are called royal, βασιλικαι /royal/, one must understand that they were called so in the past. Today we call royal the middle doors of the iconostasis, which according to ancient custom are called holy: αγιαι ΰυραι /holy doors/ (chapter 96, Greek Typikon).

265.text: According to the Slavic typikon or, speaking more precisely, according to the Pochaiv Menaion, according to the Moscow Typikon and according to the Tserkovne Oko, the Deacon sings the whole litany, and the Priest sings nothing. And the censer, which with us the Priest holds with the cross, it would be better for the Deacon to hold and cense, as the new Constantinopolitan Typikon and the Tserkovne Oko prescribe on 14 September.

266.text: From the aforesaid we see that with us, according to the Typikon of the Lviv University, the Priest turns first to the east, then to the north, after that to the west, to the south and again to the east. According to general Slavic typikons: to the east, to the west, to the south, to the north and again to the east. According to the Greek Typikon: to the east, to the south, to the west, to the north and again to the east. The new Constantinopolitan Typikon prescribes as with us.

267.text: The rule of the Triodion of the Sunday of the Veneration of the Cross prescribes for the Priest before the veneration to open the reliquary of the cross: και ανοιξας την ύηκην /and, having opened the repository/, and in the Typikon of the Lviv University: "And after the opening of the reliquary of the cross". From this it follows that they had particles of the precious Cross in monasteries. The Greek Typikon and two handwritten Slavic ones that you have, do not prescribe for the Priest to sing separately "Before Thy Cross", but for the choirs; nor to bow to the precious Cross to the ground; for only the Tserkovne Oko prescribes this on 14 September.

268.text: The Greek Typikon prescribes before the kissing of the Cross three prostrations, and after the kissing -- one; and Slavic ones -- before the kissing -- two, and after the kissing -- one; however, today we make only one before and one after the kissing. Also the Greek Typikon, having discarded both last litanies, immediately after the veneration gives the dismissal: Ψαλλομενης δε της μεγάλης δοξολογίας, αλασσει ο Ιερεύς πασαν την ιερατικην στολην, και εισέρχεται μετά του θυμιατού, προηγουμένων των λαμπάδων, εν τη αγία Τρεπεζη, και Ουμιων τον αγιον σταυρόν σταυροειδως, αίρει αυτόν μετά δίσκου επί καιφαλης, και προπορευόμενων δυο λαμπάδων, φέρει αυτόν μέχρι των βασιλικών πυλών του ναού, κακεισαι ισταται. Και πληρουμενης της δοξολογίας και του τρισάγιου, λέγει ο Ιερεύς μεγαλόφωνος: Σοφια ορθοί. Και αρχόμενα του τροπαρίου Σωσον Κύριε, και ούτως εισοδευει μετά του αγίου σταυρού, και ούτως ευτρεπισμενου τετραποδιου, τνθεται ο τίμιος σταυρός επάνω αυτού, και Ουμια ο Ιερεύς σταυροειδως. ЕІ6 ούτως βολών μετανοίας τρεις, καν ποια εστίν ήμερα, και λαβών ανά χείρας τον τιμιον σταυρόν γυμνον μετά βασιλικών κλάδων, ισταται έμπροσθεν του τετραποδιου, βλέπων κατ ανατολάς, και λέγει εις επηκοον πάντων: Ελεησον ημάς ο Θεός. Και αρχόμενα της πρώτης εκατοντάδας το Κύριε ελεησον, σφραγίζοντας του Ιερέως εν ταις εναρξεσιν μετά του αγίου σταυρού. Είτα κλίνει την καιφαλην όσον σπιύαμην από της γης, και καταμικρον ανισταται άχρι συμπληρωσεος της εκατοντάδας. Ηνικα δε φθάσει ενς το 97 Κύριε ελεησον, υψοι την φωνην ο Εκκλησιαρχης, ήγουν το Κύριε ελεησον τρις, και αισθομενος ο Ιερεύς τέλος λαμβάνειν την εκατοντάδα, σφραγίζει πάλιν τρις. Είτα στραφείς επί το νοτιον μέρος, λέγει: Ετι δεομεβα... και αρχόμενα της δευτέρας εκατοντάδας, και ποιεί ο Ιερεύς την δεύτερον υψωσιν, ως προγεγραπται. Ειύ ούτως στραφείς επί δυσμάς λέγει: Ετι δεομεθα, και αρχόμενα της τρίτης εκατοντάδας. Πληρωμένης δε αυτής, στρέφεται ο Ιερεύς επί το βορειον μέρος, και λέγει: Ετι δεομεθα... και γίνεται η τετάρτη υψωσις. Και ούτως στρέφεται ο Ιερεύς κατ ανατολάς, και λέγει: Ετι δεομεύα... και αρχομεΟα της πέμπτης εκατοντάδας. Μετά δε την πεμπτην υψωσιν ψαλλομεν το Κοντακιον Ο υψωθείς. ЕІІ9 ούτως: Τον σταυρόν σου προσκυνουμεν Δέσποτα τρεις. Ψαλλόντων δε των αδελφών, αποτι6ισιν ο Ιερεύς το τιμιον ξυλον εν τετραποδιω, και αρχόμενα προσκυνειν, ο τε Ιερεύς, και ο Προεστως, ποιουντες και μετανοίας τρεις κατενωπιον του τυμιου σταυρού, είτα ασπάζονται. Και μετά το ασπαζαστ)αι βαλλουσιν μιαν μετανοιαν; ειΰ ούτως εις τους χορούς δεξιά και αριστερά. Είτα εισέρχονται οι αδελφοί δυο δυο κατά ταξιν, και προσκυνουσι και ασπάζονται ομοίως. Ψαλλομεν δε και τα στιχηρα ιδιομελα, αχρις ουν προσκυνουσιν οι αδελφοί, εις ηχον β το Δεύτε πιστοί. Και μετά το προσκυνησαι παντός λέγει ο Ιερεύς: Σοφια, και Απολυσις /During the singing of the Great Doxology the Priest vests in all priestly vestments and proceeds with the censer, preceded by candle-bearers, to the holy table. Having censed the holy cross crosswise, he takes it with the diskos on his head and, preceded by two candle-bearers, carries it to the royal doors of the temple, remaining there. At the end of the Doxology and Trisagion, the Priest loudly exclaims: "Wisdom, attend!" and we begin the troparion "Save, O Lord". The Priest enters with the holy cross and places the precious cross on the prepared tetrapod, having censed it crosswise. Then, having bowed three times, whatever day it may be, he takes into his hands the precious cross, wrapped with basil branches, stands before the tetrapod, looking to the east, and says so that all can hear: "Have mercy on us, O God". And we begin "Lord, have mercy" of the first hundred, and the Priest at the beginning blesses with the holy cross. After this he bows his head to, approximately, a quarter of a meter from the ground and gradually rises until the end of the hundred. When "Lord, have mercy" is sung for the 97th time, the Ecclesiarch raises his voice. Then "Lord, have mercy" is sung three times, and the Priest, noticing that the hundred is coming to an end, again signs three times with the cross. Then he, having turned to the south, says: "Again we pray" and we begin the second hundred, and the Priest performs the second exaltation of the cross, as prescribed. Then, turned to the west, says: "Again we pray" and we begin the third hundred. At the end, the Priest turns to the north and says: "Again we pray" and the fourth exaltation takes place. Then the Priest turns to the east and says: "Again we pray" and we begin the fifth hundred. After the fifth exaltation we sing the Kontakion "Thou Who Wast lifted up" ("Voznesyisya"). Then "Before Thy Cross" is sung three times. While the brethren sing, the Priest places the precious cross on the tetrapod and we begin to venerate. The Priest and the Superior, having bowed three times before the precious cross, kiss it. After kissing they bow once. Also those in the choirs on the right and left. Then the brethren approach two by two, according to rank, bowing, simultaneously and kiss. We sing the stichera idiomesa, while the brethren venerate, in Tone 2 "Come, ye faithful". And when all have finished venerating, the Priest exclaims: "Wisdom!" and the dismissal follows/ (14 September).

269.text: Thus our menaia and Moscow Typikon (15 September). And when the typikons say nothing about the sequential Apostle and Gospel, then, however, they can be taken in the second place, as on the Apodosis of the feast 21 September, when it falls on a Sunday, and when -- not, then even on the Apodosis of the Exaltation not to take the sequential ones, so that there would be a certain coordination of rules.

271.text: Eparchial News. 4 September 1898, part XVI, p. 149.

272.text: Thus our Pochaiv Menaion, Tserkovne Oko and Moscow Typikon. But our liturgikons, horologia and the Greek-Venetian Menaion of 1755 prescribe to take the Service of the Holy Fathers on the Sunday following 11 October; one must understand, that when 11 October falls on a weekday; similarly in the latest Greek-Venetian Menaion (1884) and in the new Constantinopolitan Typikon, where it is prescribed to take on the very day of 11 October, if Sunday, if -- not, then on the following Sunday. What shall we say to this? We consider that all these rules are good, however, it is not good when liturgical books of one and the same church province give uncoordinated rules. For when we accept the rule of our Menaion, then let it be placed also in the liturgikons And in the horologia, for when we accept the rule of the latter, then let It be also in the Menaion. And if we adhere to the rule of the Menaion, then it is necessary to present it already on 8 October, so that, reading, one can notice about the Following Sunday. This must be understood also about the Service of the Holy Fathers of the First Six Councils on 16 July, which the menaia both ours and Greek, Prescribe to transfer back, to 13 July, if it falls on Wednesday; the Greek menaia present this not in accordance with their rule on 11 October, when they prescribe to transfer this service from 16 July back, they have to transfer it back also from 11 October. It seems to us, And it would be simpler not to transfer these services back, but to take on the very [days of] 11 October and 16 July, when they fall on Sunday, if -- not, on the following Sunday.

273.text: According to the rule of our Menaion, Moscow Typikon and Tserkovne Oko, first everything -- to the Earthquake, and then -- to the Saint. In the Greek-Venetian Menaion of 1755 Prokimenon, Apostle, Alleluia, Gospel and Communion Hymn -- only to the Saint, and in the latest, of 1884, first -- to the Saint, and afterwards -- to the Earthquake. In the new Constantinopolitan -- Troparia of the Earthquake, and everything else -- only to the Saint. According to the general Slavic typikon, which is adhered to only in cathedral churches, before the Apostle-Gospel of the Saint, the Apostle-Gospel also of the day is taken.

274.text: Thus the typikons both Greek and Slavic, but since the latter are taken from the Greek ones, which generally do not have Sunday kontakia, and Slavic ones do, we think that Slavs should take also the Sunday Kontakion alternating with the others, that is on the 1st -- Resurrectional; on the 3rd -- of the Earthquake; on the 6th -- to the Saint; on the 9th -- again Resurrectional.

275.text: According to the rule of our Menaion, Moscow Typikon and Tserkovne Oko -- / Resurrectional Troparion, of the Earthquake and of the Saint. Resurrectional Kontakion, Glory: to the Saint, Both now: of the Earthquake. Everything else -- to the Earthquake, and afterwards -- to the Saint; Apostle-Gospel -- sequential, under the Prokimenon (zaspiv). The Greek Menaion of 1755 gives nothing of the Earthquake.

276.text: It would be better to transfer it to 12 November, so that with the change of the calendar there would be no confusion in new editions of church books. For already this year, 1900, the day 31 October corresponds not to 12, but to 13 November.

277.text: Some consider, according to the edition of the Peremyshl Typikon of 1870, p. 271, that neither on St. Michael, nor on St. Prophet Elias, should "Blessed is the man" be sung and, that then not a single kathisma is taken, for this kathisma, as the publisher writes about it, is found only in the Pochaiv Anthologion, and in the most ancient menaia and Anthologia they are not mentioned; the reason for this is considered to be that "Elias did not die, and St. Michael, as bodiless, is not subject to death". However, this is not enough. For regarding the rule, not only the Pochaiv Anthologion (Anthologion) of 1777 and the Pochaiv Menaion of the same year, but also the Lviv Anthologion (Anthologion) of 1643 and the Great Typikon, under the title Tserkovne Oko, printed in Moscow in 1615, that is more than a century and a half before the Pochaiv Anthologion, and the manuscript Anthologion of 1736, which we have, and the Typikon of the All-Russian Church, printed in Moscow in 1859, by the decision of its Governing Synod, give also on these two feasts the kathisma "Blessed is the man". Although some rules, like the Moscow Menaion of 1782, the Greek-Venetian of 1884 do not give "Blessed is the man", it does not follow from this that no kathisma is needed, for even on Saints without Polyeleos in the Menaion a kathisma is not given, but the sequential one is meant; so here one can understand the sequential one, which three ancient handwritten Slavic typikons give: one -- of the Lviv University, the second -- of St. Onuphrius in Lviv, and the third -- of the library of the Chapter of St. George; also Tserkovne Oko (which gives two rules: one with "Blessed is the man", and the second with the sequential kathisma). The reason that these rules give for these two feasts a sequential kathisma, may lie in the fact that their service initially had neither All-Night Vigil nor Polyeleos, but gradually, with time, grew into All-Night Vigil. About St. Elias it is written in the Pochaiv Menaion: "Let it be known that in printed Greek menaia, in handwritten typikons, and also in Slavic handwritten and printed typikons, the service of the Prophet Elias is given on 6, with Octoechos". 337.text: Greek menaia and typikons give a rule only for two cases of Saturdays and Sundays between the Nativity and Theophany, that is: one -- for two Saturdays and two Sundays; the second -- for one Saturday and one Sunday, and for these one Saturday and one Sunday they give the following rule: Ει δε τύχη εν Σαββατον και μια Κυριακή, αναγινωσκεται τω μεν Σαββατω, Σαββατω μετά την Χρίστου γεννησιν, τη δε Κυριακή, Κυριακή προ των Φοτων /If there should happen to be one Saturday and one Sunday, on the Saturday is read that which is also on the Saturday after the Nativity of Christ, and on the Sunday that which is on the Sunday before Theophany/. And this rule is enough for the case of one Saturday with one Sunday, for then this Saturday falls during December (the 31st), and the Sunday -- during January (the 1st); however, it is not enough for one Saturday with two Sundays, nor for one Sunday with two Saturdays, for then this Saturday falls during January (the 1st), as in the seventh row, and the Sunday -- during December (the 31st), as this is in the 3rd row; and as it is not possible, according to the Greek Typikon itself, to read the Apostle-Gospel of the Sunday after the Nativity outside the feast of the Nativity, in January, but it must be transferred back, to 26 December δια το αρχήν λαμβάνειν τον Ιαννουαριον μήνα, και την των Χρίστου Γεννών εορτην αποδιδοσΟαι /because the month of January begins and the feast of the Nativity of Christ is given up/: so it is not possible to read the Apostle-Gospel of the Sunday before Theophany, within the feast of the Nativity, or the Apostle-Gospel of the Saturday after the Nativity to read in January. Therefore there is nothing strange that the Slavs supplemented their rules with what was lacking. However, the rules of our Menaion and the Russian ones, given on 26 December, for Saturdays and Sundays between the Nativity and Theophany, likely due to the negligence of copyists, in some places gave incorrectly and must be corrected, in our opinion, thus: The rule of the first case: "If the Nativity falls on a Sunday", then it should end thus: "as in the present section in the row it will appear, if the Circumcision and Basil fall on a Sunday" (as in the following case). The rule of the third case, "if the Nativity on Tuesday", then from the words: "And on Sunday" to the end, and should be: "And on Sunday, which is before Theophany, Prokimenon, Apostle, Alleluia and Gospel we read on the first day of January, as will be in the row, if the Circumcision and Basil fall on a Sunday". The rule of the fifth case from the words: "And on the second day Prokimenon, Apostle, Alleluia and Gospel we read first of the Sunday before Theophany, and then -- of the Saint" and everything that is there. 440.text: The Co-suffering of the Most Holy Theotokos can fall up to 20 July, in the case of the latest Pascha, which is 25 April. For from Pascha to the Co-suffering there will be 69 days, that is from Pascha to the Descent -- 50, from the Descent to the Sunday of All Saints and to the following Sunday (of the Eucharist) -- 14, from the second Sunday to the following Friday -- 5 days. If on 25 April there will be Pascha, then the 69th day from Pascha will be 2 July. If the last boundary of Pascha shifts three days back, then the Co-suffering will move to 29 June, and if eight days back, it will move to 24 June.

555.text: The Order of the Akathist, that is the Non-Sitting [Hymn], is sung in memory of the triple deliverance of Constantinople from the invasion of enemies, thanks to the intercession of the Mother of God, whose precious robe, brought from Jerusalem and placed by St. Pulcheria in the Blachernae church, and the Icon of the Hodegetria, painted, in the opinion of the Greeks, by St. Luke, were carried around the city, invoking her help. The first invasion was under Emperor Heraclius (reigned from 610 to 641) from the Persian army, led by the satrap Sarvar, and also from the Scythian army, under the command of the Khagan. Part of the enemies were destroyed by a small number of armed Christians who came out of the temple of the Most Holy Theotokos, and partly -- by a strong sea storm which destroyed their ships. The second invasion was 36 years later, that is under Constantine Pogonatos (668-685) and ended partly by the disease of the soldiers, and partly -- by a sea storm when they were returning home. The third was under Leo the Isaurian (717-741) and ended by a sea storm, famine, division of forces against the Bulgarians, by whom they were beaten (Synaxarion of this Saturday, about which also Nilles, Calend. vol. 2, p. 152).

607.text: This troparion is prescribed only once: Typikon of Sabbas, Greek Triodion, Greek Typikon, our Manuscript Typikon, another of Lviv University; other rubrics prescribe it twice, the second time -- with the refrain "Glory, Both now". Tserkovne Oko prescribes it first once, then Glory: the ending, Both now: whole. Obviously, all rubrics have this troparion; and the troparion "The noble Joseph", which is sung before it, is prescribed primarily by various Greek and Slavonic rubrics and the Greek Typikon of Sabbas. The sticheron "Come, let us bless" only our editions have, and the new Constantinopolitan Typikon, before the troparion "The noble Joseph" prescribes also the Resurrection Troparion "When Thou didst descend" and "The angel stood by the tomb". Before the troparion "The noble Joseph" our and Greek rubrics prescribe: "Let us attend. Peace be to all. Wisdom, let us attend", others Slavonic -- only "Wisdom, Aright"; and since they do not prescribe here "The noble Joseph", they prescribe "Wisdom, Aright" to exclaim before the Troparion of the Prophecy. Tserkovne Oko prescribes "Wisdom, Aright" before "The noble Joseph", and before the Troparion of the Prophecy: "Let us attend. Peace to Thee. Wisdom, let us attend". The Entrance, according to the Russian rubric, takes place in the following way: "Then the Superior enters the holy altar with the priests and deacons, vests in all sacred vestments, and the priests -- only in phelonia, comes out with the Gospel under the Shroud, with priests who support, and deacons who cense. At this time ringing is done with all might. He is preceded with candles and with two candlesticks, and both choirs sing the funeral Trisagion. The Abbot, having come before the holy royal doors, stands here, awaiting the conclusion of the last Trisagion. When it ends, the Superior with the Gospel enters the royal doors and places the Gospel on the altar, and the Shroud -- on the prepared table, in the form of a tomb. In monasteries, after the dismissal, the kissing of the Shroud, placed in the tomb, takes place". This is -- the Moscow Typikon. In the Patriarchate of Constantinople it takes place thus: "Great Doxology. Then we begin the sung [Trisagion], preceding the Epitaphios, and going out of the temple, the Entrance takes place, as is customary; as soon as we return, the Patriarch enters directly into the holy sanctuary, with the rest, and immediately exclaims 'Let us attend. Peace be to all. Wisdom'. And the Troparion 'When Thou didst descend' is sung. He censes around the holy table, preceded by the Epitaphios, then 'The angel stood by the tomb' up to 'appeared as a stranger'. After this is sung 'The noble Joseph', up to 'wrapped, laid', and they place the Epitaphios on the holy table. At once the canonarch from outside reads the Troparion, the Prophecy and the Apostle, and the Gospel is said by the Patriarch, in front of the Gate" (New Constantinopolitan Typikon). In various parts of Greece, according to the testimony of Allatius, the procession takes place in the following way: "The custom prevailed, that, while Ps. 118 is sung, and at individual verses individual Troparia are sung, Christ beautifully carved, or skillfully painted on a board, and placed in a bier, with a solemn apparatus of burning candles, Priests, dressed as when they celebrate the sacred solemnities of Masses, the rest of the Clergy accompanying not without order, and the faithful of Christ following the bier through the streets of the city, is carried, and set forth to all to be adored, and kissed: and thus is open to the veneration of all. Meanwhile flowers placed on the image, are sought by all with the greatest zeal, which they promise to themselves for the greatest good, not only of the body, but of domestic affairs" (Nil). Kalend. vol. 2, p. 241).

630.text: In the Rite of the Panagia, given in the Horologion before or after the 9th Hour, it is recounted how the apostles after Christ's Resurrection, before the dispersion throughout the whole world, stayed together in Jerusalem, having the custom to dine together and at this time to leave at the table an empty place, on which they placed a pillow, and on it -- : a piece of bread in Christ's portion, that is in memory of Jesus Christ, and after dinner they elevated the piece, saying: "Glory to Thee, O Christ God, help us"; from the Resurrection to the Ascension: "Christ is risen". When the apostles did this after the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos, she appeared to them in the air alive, in light radiance, surrounded by angels, saying: "Rejoice, for I am with you all days". And they frightened, instead of "Glory to Thee, O Christ God", exclaimed "All-holy (Panagia) Theotokos, help us". This rite of the Panagia, named so from the name Panagia /All-holy/, by which the apostles invoked then the Most Holy Theotokos, imitating the apostles, was repeated once by the Emperor in the Court... and by people in churches or homes, and predominantly daily in monasteries, as is seen from the service of the meal, given in the Horologion, however, more solemnly -- in Bright Week, in which not a piece of bread, which they ate, but a whole (whole) bread they offered on all days of the week, not eating until Bright Saturday, but only kissing it. And this rite was initially served only at the meal, as it is in the Greek Pentecostarion. The Slavs, for the sake of greater solemnity, did not serve the whole rite only at the meal, but daily, throughout the whole Bright Week, preceded by lights and the icon of the Resurrection carried the Artos from the church to the meal and from the meal to the church, to the sounds of bells, as for Tserkovne Oko has our Pochaiv Triodion and Russian Typika. Today this rite is celebrated among us only in Bright Week and not with all prayers and rites, as the Triodion gives, but only as here, in the text, we gave, however, not only in monasteries, but also in all other churches. The prayers for the blessing and breaking of the Artos the Slavs added to themselves, for in Greek books they are not encountered; the prayer for breaking is not given even in Slavonic rubrics, except ours, but others break it without prayer.

763.text:
These gifts are arranged according to such a scheme so that the blessing of the priest depicts upon them the sign of the cross: loaf • wine • • oil • wheat **Chunk 74** **IV. Rubric of Matins in Sundays and Feasts** **1. In Concelebration of One Deacon** **74.** If before this there was no Vigil, then Matins begins thus^[764]: **75.** The priest puts on the *ryasa* the epitrachelion, having previously blessed it, goes before the holy doors and begins: "Blessed is our God." Choir: "Amen," "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee," "O Heavenly King," Trisagion, "Most Holy Trinity," "Our Father." Priest: "For Thine is the kingdom." Choir: "Amen," "Lord, have mercy" (12), "Glory, Both now," "Come, let us worship" (3). The priest enters the sanctuary through the southern doors, recites the Prayer of the Censer, takes the censer, censes the throne from the four sides, the icon behind the altar and other icons of the sanctuary. Then he goes out of the sanctuary through the northern doors, comes before the holy doors and, bowing, censes the icons of the southern part of the iconostasis, beginning from the image of the Savior, the icons of the northern part, beginning from the icon of the Theotokos, then -- the choirs, right and left. He censes the people either from the solea or crossing the whole temple, while the choir reads the 20th(19th) Psalm "The Lord hear thee" and the 21st(20th) "The King shall joy." When the choir begins the Trisagion, the priest returns before the holy doors, censes them and after "Our Father" exclaims: "For Thine is the kingdom," enters the sanctuary through the southern doors, stands before the holy table and, after the completion of the troparia "O Lord, save Thy people," exclaims the Litany for Emperors. After the exclamation "For a merciful," Choir: "Amen," "In the name of the Lord, bless, father." The priest exclaims^[765]: "Glory to the Holy, Consubstantial." Choir: "Amen," "Glory to God in the highest" (3) with small bows and "O Lord, open my lips" (2). The Six Psalms are read. **76.** During the reading of the Six Psalms^[766] the priest, standing before the holy table, begins to recite the Matins Prayers. After the first three psalms, he goes out through the northern doors and, having stood before the holy doors, continues to read the Matins Prayers. After the completion of the psalms, the priest responds to the bow of the deacon and, having returned through the southern doors into the sanctuary, stands before the holy table. At the end of the Six Psalms, the deacon, dressed in the sticharion with the orarion, goes out through the northern doors, pays respect to the priest, stands on his usual place and exclaims the Great Litany. The priest exclaims: "For to Thee belongs." During the singing by the choir of "God is the Lord," the deacon recites the verses and, after a small bow, returns through the southern doors into the sanctuary. **77.** After the Troparia, the reader reads the regular Kathisma, after which the deacon [exclaims] before the holy doors -- the Small Litany, and the priest exclaims: "For Thine is the dominion." Then the reader reads the second regular Kathisma, the deacon -- the second Small Litany, and the priest -- the exclamation "For Thou art a good God." After the Troparia "The Angelic Council," if it is Sunday, or after the Magnification [*Velychannya*], if it is a feast, the deacon again reads the Small Litany, and the priest exclaims: "For blessed." **78.** After the Gradual [*Stepenna*], the holy doors are opened, and the deacon approaches the holy doors and, looking at the people, exclaims: "Let us be attentive." The priest, dressed in the phelonion, blesses the people: "Peace be to all." Deacon: "Wisdom, let us be attentive." The choir sings the Prokimenon. Deacon: "Let us pray to the Lord." Choir: "Lord, have mercy." The priest exclaims: "For Holy art Thou, our God." The deacon censes the holy table from the four sides and everything else, according to custom (see no. 33). Choir: "Let everything that has breath praise the Lord." The deacon recites both verses, and the choir repeats: "Let everything that has breath," after which the deacon: "And that we may be vouchsafed." Choir: "Lord, have mercy" (3). The priest takes the Gospel, goes out before the holy doors, stands at a slight distance before them on the solea, places the Gospel on the analogion and reads it, turned to the people. Deacon: "Wisdom, arise, let us hear the Holy Gospel," and the priest blesses: "Peace be to all." Choir: "And to thy spirit." Priest: "The reading from the Holy Gospel according to (Name)." Deacon: "Let us be attentive." The priest reads the Matins Gospel. **79.** After the reading, the priest kisses the closed book and carries it to the middle of the temple, where he places it on the tetrapod, and he himself returns through the holy doors into the sanctuary. The deacon reads "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ," if it is Sunday, or the reader -- the 50th Psalm "Have mercy on me, O God." After the sticheron, the deacon [is] at his usual place: "O God, save Thy people." Choir: "Lord, have mercy" (12) and the priest exclaims: "By the grace and compassions." Choir: "Amen." The Canon begins. The holy doors, if there was no Vigil, are closed. **80.** If there was a Vigil, the priest after the exclamation "By the grace," holding the cross in his hands, goes out through the holy [doors], and the deacon with the oil, blessed at Vespers, and the anointing brush, -- through the northern doors and they stand on the right side of the tetrapod. There the priest anoints crosswise the forehead of everyone who approaches to kiss the Holy Gospel. After the completion of the anointing [*Myrovanne*] they return to the sanctuary: the priest -- through the holy, and the deacon -- through the southern doors and, having closed the holy doors, the priest takes off the phelonion. **81.** After the third and sixth Odes, the deacon sings the Small Litany either before the holy doors, or near the tetrapod, if the anointing was not yet finished, and the priest exclaims the exclamation either from the sanctuary, or from the tetrapod. After the singing of the Katavasia of the eighth Ode, the deacon takes the censer and, having stood before the icon of the Theotokos, says: "The Theotokos and Mother of Light let us magnify in songs" and, having returned through the southern doors into the sanctuary, censes the holy table from four sides and everything else, according to the prescription (see no. 33). After the ninth Ode and after the recitation by the choir of "It is truly meet," if it is not Sunday, but if it is Sunday or a feast, after the singing of the Heirmos, the deacon exclaims from his place the Small Litany. The priest exclaims: "For all the powers of heaven praise Thee." The choir sings the Exaposteilarion. **82.** After the Praises stichera, at "Glory," the deacon opens the holy doors. The priest in the phelonion stands before the throne, the deacon stands to his right and, after the completion of the last sticheron, the priest, turned to the east, exclaims: "Glory to Thee, who hast shown us the Light." The Great Doxology is sung. Then, also according to custom, the Troparion is recited, and the priest, preceded by the deacon, carries the Holy Gospel from the tetrapod into the sanctuary and places it on the holy table. **83.** After this, the deacon stands at his usual place and exclaims the litanies "Have mercy on us, O God" and "Let us complete." The priest blesses the people and exclaims: "Peace be to all." Choir: "And to thy spirit." Deacon: "Bow your heads unto the Lord." Choir: "To Thee, O Lord." The priest recites quietly the prayer "O Holy Lord," after which he exclaims: "For Thine it is." The dismissal follows, which the deacon begins: "Wisdom" (see no. 36). **84.** After the dismissal, the reader immediately begins the 1st Hour: "Come, let us worship" (3) and the psalms. After "Our Father," the priest in the epitrachelion: "For Thine is the kingdom." Reader -- Kontakion and "Lord, have mercy" (40). The priest goes out of the sanctuary through the northern doors and before the holy [doors], turned to the east, loudly: "Thou who at all times". Reader: "Lord, have mercy" (3), "Glory, Both now", "More honorable than the Cherubim", "In the name of the Lord, bless, father." Priest: "God be merciful to us." Reader: "Amen." Priest recites the prayer "O Christ, the True Light", "Glory to Thee, O Christ God." Reader: "Glory, Both now", "Lord, have mercy" (3), "Bless." The priest imparts the Small Dismissal, returns into the sanctuary and takes off the epitrachelion. **2. In Concelebration of Two Deacons** **85.** At the end of the Six Psalms, the 1st deacon goes out through the northern doors and exclaims the Great Litany, as well as the verses at "God is the Lord" and, having made a small bow, returns into the sanctuary through the southern doors. After the first Kathisma the 2nd deacon, and after the second Kathisma the 1st deacon, sing the Small Litany. After the Troparia "The Angelic Council" or after the Magnifications, the 2nd deacon likewise sings the Small Litany. After the Gradual [*Stepenna*], the 1st deacon: "Let us be attentive." Priest: "Peace be to all." 2nd deacon: "Wisdom, let us be attentive." 1st deacon: "Let us pray to the Lord." Both deacons cense the holy table, the iconostasis, the choirs and the people, as noted in the rubric of Vespers in concelebration with two deacons (see no. 40). At "Let everything that has breath," the 1st deacon recites the first verse, and the 2nd deacon -- the second. **86.** For the anointing of the faithful, the 1st deacon goes out with the priest, and the 2nd exclaims the Small Litany after the third Ode, and also -- after the sixth Ode. After the Katavasia of the eighth Ode, the 1st deacon takes the censer, goes out through the northern doors, stands before the icon of the Theotokos and calls: "The Theotokos and Mother of Light," then returns through the southern doors into the sanctuary and, together with the 2nd deacon, censes the throne and everything else, as noted above (see no. 39), and after the censing they return into the sanctuary: the 1st deacon -- through the southern, and the 2nd -- through the northern doors. After the ninth Ode, the 1st deacon exclaims the Small Litany. **87.** After the Praises stichera, the holy doors are opened. The 1st deacon stands before the holy table to the right of the priest, and the 2nd -- to the left. After the Great Doxology, all, having made a small bow, go to the tetrapod, the priest takes the Holy Gospel and, preceded by the deacons, returns into the sanctuary. **88.** After this, the deacons go out: the 1st deacon exclaims the first litany "Have mercy on us, O God," and the 2nd -- the second "Let us complete." 1st deacon: "Bow your heads unto the Lord." The dismissal follows, which the 1st deacon begins: "Wisdom" (see no. 36, note). **3. Without a Deacon** **89.** A priest who serves Matins without a deacon does and says everything that belongs to the deacon, considering this: **90.** After the completion of the Six Psalms, he does not return into the sanctuary, but, standing before the holy doors, exclaims the Great Litany and its exclamation: "For to Thee belongs," as well as the verses during the singing by the choir of "God is the Lord." After the completion of this, he makes a small bow and returns through the southern doors into the sanctuary. It should be noted that when the priest does not have enough time to recite all the Matins Prayers before the iconostasis, he may finish them in the sanctuary during the reading of the Kathismata. After the Prokimenon, he himself exclaims: "Let us pray to the Lord"; reads the verses at "Let everything that has breath"; before the reading of the Gospel, exclaims: "Let us be attentive," and after the Gospel reads "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ." After the 3rd and 6th Odes of the Canon -- Small Litanies and exclaims from the throne or from the place where he anoints. After the anointing, he returns through the holy doors into the sanctuary and takes off the phelonion. **91.** After the Katavasia of the 8th Ode, he goes out in the epitrachelion through the northern doors, stands before the icon of the Theotokos and calls: "The Theotokos and Mother of Light," then censes, as noted above (see no. 33). After the censing, he returns through the southern doors into the sanctuary, exclaims the Small Litany and its exclamation. **92.** After the Praises stichera, at "Glory," he puts on the phelonion, opens the holy doors and, after the last sticheron, exclaims: "Glory to Thee, who hast shown us the Light." Everything else takes place as was presented (see nos. 82-83). **93.** After the dismissal, the priest closes the holy doors, takes off the phelonion and the 1st Hour begins. **4. In Concelebration of Priests** **94.** Concelebrants, in an even number, put on epitrachelia over their *ryasas* and put on phelons during the reading of the Kathisma and stand on the sides of the holy table, as at Vespers (see no. 50). During the singing of the Polyeleos, all go out, having made a small bow, through the holy doors, having lowered the phelonion and hands down, in front -- the younger ones. Two first ones carry the icon of the feast or saint, if it has not yet been placed on the left side of the tetrapod between both choirs, and place it on the tetrapod; all stand on the sides of the tetrapod in two rows, facing one another, the principal celebrant stands in the middle before the tetrapod, and to his right -- the deacon. **

[INSERT DIAGRAM/TABLE HERE FROM ORIGINAL PDF]

Diagram: At the Magnification** [Left Column] Candle-bearer ... 6 ... 4 ... 2 ... Concelebrants [Center] TETRAPOD [Right Column] Candle-bearer ... 5 ... 3 ... 1 ... Concelebrants [Bottom] Celebrant ... Deacon **95.** Then all sing the Magnification. When the choir repeats the Magnification, the priest, preceded by the deacon with a lighted candle, censes from four sides the icon of the feast or saint on the tetrapod, the holy table, the sanctuary, the iconostasis, the concelebrants, both choirs, the people and once more the icon of the feast, but only from the front. If, however, the usual censing takes place before the Gospel, then at the Magnification the priest censes only the icon itself. Choir: "Glory" and again the Magnification. Then the celebrant and concelebrants sing the Magnification once more. **96.** After the Magnifications all, the younger ones -- in front, return through the holy doors into the sanctuary before the holy table. After the Gospel all, having made a small bow, depart and take off their vestments. **Shortening of Matins**^[767] **1. Beginning** -- The priest, having put on the epitrachelion, censes as usual (see at "Lord, I have cried," no. 75). -- Then he exclaims: "Glory to the Holy," and the choir recites everything else and the 142nd Psalm on Sunday or the regular one -- on feasts. -- After the Great Litany -- "God is the Lord," Troparion of the Sunday or Feast, Theotokion according to the tone of the Troparion. **2. Sung Kathismata** -- Regular Kathismata with Sessional Hymns are not taken, but sung ones are taken thus: "The Angelic Council" -- only on Sundays, "Praise the name of the Lord" (Polyeleos) -- only on feasts, "By the waters of Babylon" -- only on the Sundays of Great Lent. -- The priest at the appointed time puts on the phelonion, opens the holy doors and exclaims: "Peace be to all." Then he censes. If there was censing at the Magnification, then before the Reading of the Gospel there will be no censing. -- Prokimenon, "Let everything that has breath" -- according to the tone of the season. **3. Bringing out the Gospel** -- The priest, having read the Gospel, carries the Holy Book out to the tetrapod, accompanied by two candle-bearers. -- The Reader, if there is no deacon, reads "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ." -- All go to kiss the Gospel. If there was a *Litiya*, then the anointing takes place (see no. 80). -- Having returned to the throne, the priest recites the prayer "O God, save." After this he does not close the holy doors in view of the shortening of Matins. **4. Magnification of the Theotokos** -- Having recited the prayer "O God, save," the priest takes the censer and goes out before the icon of the Theotokos. -- There he exclaims: "The Theotokos and Mother of Light," censes the icon, then returns into the sanctuary and censes everything, as usual. -- The choir sings "More honorable than the Cherubim" at the beginning and at the end of the verses, which both choirs recite alternately. **5. Laudatory Prayers** -- Psalms 148, 149 and 150 are sung singly, in turn. -- After "Most Blessed" the priest exclaims: "Glory to Thee, who hast shown us the Light." At the Great Doxology there will be no censing. -- During the singing of the Troparion, the priest carries the Gospel back, and after the completion -- immediately says the dismissal. **Beginning of Paschal Matins** At Paschal Matins the censing takes place with special solemnity. The servers, having put on the best vestments, as at the Divine Liturgy, go out before the throne in the usual order and make a bow all together. The principal celebrant gives the Gospel to the 1st server, and to the 2nd -- the icon of the Resurrection of Christ, he himself takes the cross with his left hand, and with the right (from the deacon) -- the censer. He censes first the throne, and afterwards -- the servers. Then the principal celebrant, having given the censer to the deacon, stands at his place. All bow before the throne and turn to the east to go out to the narthex. The exit takes place according to the usual order of seniority under the peeling of bells and with the singing of the hymn "Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior." And the order is such: candle-bearers, priests, deacons with lighted candles, and behind them -- the principal celebrant. All are also given lighted candles. In the narthex all stand before the closed church doors, as in the

diagram below: **Church doors** **___________I_______I__________** **Left Kliros** ...................................... **Right Kliros** **A2** ..................................................... **A1** **C4** ..................................................... **C3** **C2** ..................................................... **C1** **D2** **PC** **D1** **People** Here the principal celebrant takes the censer from the deacon and censes the icons of the narthex, the kliroses and the people. The deacon precedes him the entire time with a lighted candle. Then the principal celebrant returns before the doors and censes the deacon; and then the latter, having taken the censer from the principal celebrant, censes him and immediately gives the censer back to the principal celebrant, who thrice censes the doors and then exclaims: "Glory to the Holy." After "Amen," the principal celebrant with the concelebrants sings thrice "Christ is risen" and the verses "Let God arise," to which the people respond with the song "Christ is risen." After the last "Christ is risen," the principal celebrant opens the doors (Among us he knocks thrice with the cross) and enters the church, and behind him all the servers and people (see no. 71; Liturgicon, pp. 141-146).
